workflow_blockers: generic repository test job installs no torch while collecting existing spatial tests that import torch
repository-wide Ruff has pre-existing findings in unrelated legacy files

expert_selection_methodology: candidate-library admission uses peer-reviewed capability evidence, modality/input-dimensionality scope, released native interface, and weight/audit availability
per-expert source qualification estimates action prevalence, conditional precision, utility, and harm separately
portfolio selection replays feasible verifier subsets on a disjoint source-P set to measure non-additive interactions
leave-one-out and excluded-expert add-back explicitly measure whether disabling or restoring an expert improves source utility
runtime can select the empty portfolio and exactly preserve the immutable Generalist
qualification, portfolio selection and fresh canary are group/image-disjoint
target/test labels are forbidden for expert selection, threshold changes or portfolio changes
notes: The previous Tx-v2 source diagnosis showed that per-expert qualification alone cannot establish useful collaboration when source utility is non-positive or interactions are harmful.
The v3 portfolio is a source-only policy for deciding which qualified verifiers may run together; it is not a target-trained gate.
Research-roadmap models do not count as active coverage until their exact input/runtime contracts and source qualification are validated.
MUSK and MONET configuration presence does not grant authority; both still require real checkpoint/runtime and source qualification validation.
This report records engineering/protocol validation only and makes no new benchmark gain claim.
